title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.19893v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Where does the novelty a base language model produces with no task come from, and what can an LLM judge of a long stream actually see? We dismantle a cognitively inspired generation loop over 24 conditions on three base models. Most of its effect lives in one operation: a new subject injected every few hundred tokens (an interruption) into a stream whose literal repetition is damped (habituation). We judge windows of generated text only, with the premise as the unit (n=10) and a judge measured for repeatability, against a second judge family and against human readers. Under that protocol the interruption raises judged surprise by 1.2 to 1.4 points and connection by 0.8 over habituation alone. A connective that asks for continuity hurts; a bare paragraph break adds nothing detectable on fresh text; a reset context does at least as well as a kept one; and a pre-registered replication on new premises confirms the primary contrast. translated_title: 打断循环：周期性主题变化提升基础语言模型的评判惊喜度与连贯性
translated_abstract: 摘要：一个基础语言模型在没有任务的情况下产生的新颖性从何而来，而一个LLM评判者能从长文本流中真正看到什么？我们在三个基础模型上，通过24种条件拆解了一个认知启发的生成循环。其大部分效果集中在一个操作上：每隔几百个标记注入一个新主题（打断），进入一个字面重复被抑制（习惯化）的文本流。我们仅评判生成的文本窗口，以命题为单位（n=10），并使用一个经过可重复性测量的评判者，与第二个评判者家族及人类读者进行比较。在该协议下，打断使评判惊喜度比单独习惯化提高了1.2至1.4分，连贯性提高了0.8分。一个要求连续性的连接词会损害效果；一个单独的段落分隔符在新文本上没有可检测的附加效果；重置上下文至少与保留上下文效果相当；并且一项预先注册的复制实验在新命题上确认了主要对比。
tldr: 该论文发现，在基础语言模型的生成循环中，周期性注入新主题（打断）是提升文本评判惊喜度和连贯性的核心机制，且效果显著优于仅靠习惯化或其他操作。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that periodically injecting new subjects (interruptions) into a base language model's generation loop is the core mechanism that boosts judged surprise and connection, significantly outperforming habituation alone or other operations.
